title: camera sources, vault passwords and per-person access (manual until automated)

clauses.text: A network camera's password is kept in the owner's vault, not in its address, and editing never shows it.

steps.do: Add an RTSP or HTTP camera with its password, save it, then edit it.
steps.expect: The edit form shows the clean address and no password.

clauses.text: An address typed as user:password@ is split on save, and the password goes to the vault.

steps.do: Add a camera with its address typed as user:password@host and save it.
steps.expect: The saved address and the camera list show no password.

clauses.text: A shared camera shows Needs password when the owner's vault is not open.

steps.do: With the owner signed out, sign in as a listed person and open the CAMERAS tile.
steps.expect: The shared camera shows Needs password.

clauses.text: The owner and listed people watch; administrators manage without watching; others do not see the camera.

steps.do: Sign in as a listed person, then as an administrator who is not on the list, then as someone else.
steps.expect: The listed person sees and watches the camera. The administrator can manage it but not see its picture. The other person does not see it.

clauses.text: An H.264 camera shows Needs video add-on until the add-on is installed.

steps.do: Look at the tile of an H.264 camera before the video add-on is installed.
steps.expect: The camera shows Needs video add-on.

clauses.text: A dropped camera is tried again after a pause that grows.

steps.do: Unplug a network camera's cable for half a minute, plug it back in, and watch its tile.
steps.expect: The tile shows lost with the reason, then tries again and goes live. The pauses between tries grow.

clauses.text: A stream stops when nobody looks at it (about 8 seconds after the last look).

steps.do: Look at a network camera, then leave the tile.
steps.expect: The tile stops drawing the camera, and the stream stops within a few seconds.
